## Submitting

Call submit_patch as soon as you have a plausible fix, even a partial one,
and call it again after every improvement. submit_patch does not count
against your tool-call budget and costs you nothing. If you run out of
context or time, the last submitted patch is what gets scored — an early
mediocre patch always beats losing your work.

## Scratch files

Write any reproduction or debugging script to /tmp, never inside /workspace.
Everything left in /workspace becomes part of your submitted patch.
Do not modify test files, conftest.py or pytest.ini — those changes are
stripped before grading, so editing them wastes tool calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

Start with grep:
  run_command("grep -rn '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")
Read files only after grep has narrowed the candidates. Keep read_file
ranges tight — each call returns at most 150 lines and consumes context
you will need later.

from fastapi import FastAPI, Body
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import pytest

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/strict")
async def strict_endpoint(data: dict = Body(..., strict_content_type=True)):
    return data

@app.post("/not-strict")
async def not_strict_endpoint(data: dict = Body(..., strict_content_type=False)):
    return data

client = TestClient(app)

def test_strict_content_type_true_with_header():
    # Should work with application/json
    response = client.post("/strict", json={"foo": "bar"})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"foo": "bar"}

def test_strict_content_type_true_without_header():
    # Should fail (or not be parsed as JSON) if header is missing
    # When strict_content_type=True and no header, json_body remains Undefined.
    # Then body = body_bytes.
    # Then it's passed to the validator.
    # If it's a dict, Pydantic will try to validate body_bytes (bytes) as a dict, which should fail.
    response = client.post("/strict", content='{"foo": "bar"}', headers={})
    assert response.status_code == 422

def test_strict_content_type_false_without_header():
    # Should work even if header is missing
    response = client.post("/not-strict", content='{"foo": "bar"}', headers={})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"foo": "bar"}

def test_strict_content_type_true_with_wrong_header():
    # Should fail if header is not application/json
    response = client.post("/strict", content='{"foo": "bar"}', headers={"content-type": "text/plain"})
    assert response.status_code == 422

def test_strict_content_type_false_with_wrong_header():
    # Should also fail if header is present but wrong
    response = client.post("/not-strict", content='{"foo": "bar"}', headers={"content-type": "text/plain"})
    assert response.status_code == 422
